scores.rationale: Mixed tins of badges with WWI Tasmanian Wattle Day items and a Rising Sun; local collectors, but mostly common smalls in worn condition.
Eleven pre-1890 hallmarked sterling teaspoons, roughly 150g of antique silver, likely $200-300 as a set.
Heavy-looking boxed bracelet from Hobart jeweller, but no sterling mark seen so silver claim is unproven; likely $100-200.
1913 German 5 Mark (.900) mounted on a chain claimed 835; mostly silver weight, mounting hurts coin value, around $100-150.
Post-1953 anodised Australian Army badges in a bag; common, modest collector value of $30-80.
Plated advertising vesta with racehorse photo and wool broker name; worn, niche Australiana appeal, about $50-100.
LEGO 76328 Batmobile retired adult set, resale about $200-250 if sealed, discounted for scuffed box and unconfirmed seals.
Genuine-looking early incised H McHugh pot with provenance, but multiple rim chips; about $80-150.
Super7 24 inch Super Shogun Optimus Prime variant, active resale market around $250-350.
threezero DLX Bumblebee die-cast figure, secondhand resale probably $150-250.
